title: Most Drivers Cannot Pass This Motorcycle Drivers Test
summary: Ten worldwide road-safety questions test whether your driving instincts transfer to two wheels.

landing.intro: Driving a car is not enough. These 10 motorcycle questions expose the safety details most road users miss.

about.body:
This worldwide-English entertainment quiz tests broad motorcycle-safety principles that apply across many road systems. It avoids country-specific signs, licence rules, speed limits and legal wording.

Choose the safest general response in each situation. Real motorcycles, roads and local laws vary, so always follow your official rider handbook, training and the manufacturer's instructions.

Passing this quiz does not demonstrate practical riding skill or replace approved motorcycle instruction.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Choose the safest general answer from the four options.
Reveal your score and full answer review after question ten.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. Not a licensing test or a substitute for professional rider training and local road rules.

stage-1.preAdCopy: Your motorcycle-safety score and complete answer review are ready.

profile-1.title: The Roadcraft Expert
profile-1.copy: You spotted the machine, road and rider risks with exceptional consistency. Your answers reflect calm observation and strong safety instincts.

profile-2.title: The Alert Rider
profile-2.copy: Your road awareness transferred well to two wheels. Only one or two motorcycle-specific details prevented a flawless run.

profile-3.title: The Developing Rider
profile-3.copy: You recognised many of the major hazards, but a few two-wheel decisions need closer attention. The answer review shows where.

profile-4.title: The Four-Wheel Thinker
profile-4.copy: Some safe driving instincts carried across, but motorcycles add balance, visibility and braking factors that cars can hide.

profile-5.title: The Training Ground
profile-5.copy: This challenge exposed how different two-wheel roadcraft can be. Use the review as a starting point, not as practical riding instruction.

score.passed: You passed the motorcycle driver test!

motorbike-q1.question: When is tyre pressure usually best checked for an accurate routine reading?

motorbike-q2.question: Where should a rider generally direct their vision while travelling through a bend?
answers: Through the bend towards the intended path
At the edge of the road

motorbike-q3.question: Rain begins during a ride. What should happen to the space behind the vehicle ahead?
answers: It should stay exactly the same
It matters only at high speed

motorbike-q4.question: On a modern motorcycle in a straight-line emergency stop, which broad technique is generally safest?
answers: Use only the front brake instantly
Apply both brakes progressively while keeping the motorcycle stable

motorbike-q5.question: Which habit best helps reduce the chance of another driver overlooking a motorcycle?
answers: Stay out of blind spots and position for visibility
Ride beside a vehicle for as long as possible
Assume eye contact means the driver has seen you

motorbike-q6.question: What important change should a rider expect when carrying a passenger?
answers: The motorcycle will turn and stop exactly the same
Balance, acceleration and braking distance may change
The passenger should lean opposite the rider

motorbike-q7.question: How should a rider cross wet painted markings when they cannot be avoided?
answers: Keep the motorcycle as upright and smooth as possible

motorbike-q8.question: Before changing position into an area a mirror may not show, what final observation is valuable?
answers: A glance at the speed display
A look at the front wheel
A check of the fuel level
A direct blind-spot check when it is safe

motorbike-q9.question: Where should a rider find the correct drive-chain adjustment specification for their motorcycle?
answers: A guess based on another motorcycle

motorbike-q10.question: A rider notices their concentration fading on a long journey. What is the safest response?
answers: Stop somewhere safe and take a proper break
